judgements.why: On identity the two candidates are almost tied. They differ by only a few pixels, and the largest differences are the ear studs. On both, the FRONT, LEFT PROFILE and THREE-QUARTER heads are traced from the V13 heads: an edge overlay matches V13 almost line for line in cheekbones, square jaw, straight nose and eye placement. All five faces on each sheet read as the same man. Both drift the same way from V13: smoother airbrushed skin that is about 10 percent lighter and more orange, a slightly younger look, and a bulkier moustache (the moustache was requested). The TURBAN face is a fresh drawing but stays in family. The tie breaks on the ear: f2-1's full-figure ornament is a large ball on the lower edge of the lobe that reads as a small drop, and its other studs are oversized. f2-2's studs are tiny and centred on the lobe in every view, as fix2 asked. f2-2's skin tone is also marginally closer to V13. Before adoption, the author should know two things that are the same on both: the dark smudge under the lower lip is still there in THREE-QUARTER, and the LEFT FOREARM panel's right border has a sliver of sleeve left over from the mirror. Neither changes who the man is, so f2-2 is safe to adopt.

judgements.why: The two candidates share layout, costume, label text and the mirrored LEFT FOREARM panel. Header 'NAGOJI SAWANT', subtitle 'COMMANDER YEARS' and all five labels are spelled exactly, with no extra text. The background is pale ivory with no scenery, and the hair is long, curly and black with no grey and no topknot. The tunic is a buttonless wrap with sleeves to the wrists, and the talwar is at his left hip. The mirrored forearm is now correctly a left arm, palm up, with a symbol-free pale brand and a thin white scar beside it. The deciding rule is the ear ornament. In f2-1 the full-figure stud is a gold ball overhanging the lower edge of the lobe, which reads as a hanging ball, and the TURBAN stud is a low teardrop. In f2-2 every stud is a small, round, flush, mid-lobe stud with nothing below it. Both still break fix2 item 1: a dark soul-patch-like smudge under the lower lip in FRONT, THREE-QUARTER, TURBAN and the full figure. Both also share a tan border artifact at the top-right of the LEFT FOREARM panel and a bare left lobe in FRONT that contradicts the stud in LEFT PROFILE. Adopt f2-2. Before locking it, a local retouch is recommended: clear the under-lip smudge in those four views and redraw the forearm panel's right border as a plain ruled line.

judgements.why: The two candidates are nearly pixel-identical. A diff shows only re-render noise around hair and edges, and the LEFT FOREARM panel is the same in both. On identity, both read as the V13 Nagoji about ten years on. The bone structure holds (broad cheekbones, square jaw, straight nose, brown almond eyes, thick curled handlebar), and all five heads on each sheet show the same man, with mid-to-late-30s age and a leaner face as the prompt asked. The main drift from V13 is heavier, flatter brows that give a fixed scowl, a slightly longer and pointier nose in profile, and a cleaner cel-shaded finish. This drift is tolerable and is the same on both. Neither candidate fully passes the rules. Both are missing the stud on UNIFORM, show grey at only one temple in FRONT, carry a grey sweep wider than a finger in LEFT PROFILE and the main figure, have extra nape curls, a dark patch under the lower lip in FRONT, and a faint X sheen on the medallion. All labels are spelled exactly and there is no extra text. f2-2 wins by a small margin. Its under-lip shadow is a little softer, and its UNIFORM head carries the same cheek mole as FRONT and THREE-QUARTER, which helps consistency across the sheet. If the panel pipeline cannot tolerate the missing UNIFORM stud or the FRONT chin shadow, a small local fix on f2-2 for those two points is the cheapest way to close them.

judgements.why: The two sheets are almost identical. The LEFT FOREARM panel, the labels and the costume are the same in both, and the pixel differences are concentrated in the heads. Both get all the text exactly right: NAGOJI SAWANT, ANANTHAN PILLAI, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, THREE-QUARTER, UNIFORM and LEFT FOREARM, with no extra text. Both also meet these rules: a flush gold stud with nothing hanging in the main figure, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE and THREE-QUARTER; a black topknot on the crown in every head; no turban; a plain cream tube mundu with no gold border; the shoulder cloth on the left shoulder; the ivory knife; the correct uniform with the chain over the coat and no hat; a plain ivory background; and a true left forearm, palm up, with a shapeless brand that carries no symbol. f2-2 wins on two locks that fix2 named explicitly. Its main medallion is plain, while f2-1 shows an X-shaped sheen. Its FRONT head shows grey at both temples, while f2-1 shows grey at one only. Its under-lip shadow is also slightly lighter. Both share the same remaining faults: no visible stud in UNIFORM, curls hanging down the neck, a temple streak a little wider than a finger, a thinner moustache in profile, and a brand that looks blistered. These are minor enough to state as prompt caveats when f2-2 is attached. A touch-up adding the UNIFORM ear stud and removing the stray UNIFORM cheek mole would make it clean.

judgements.why: Both candidates come from the same pass. Their COURT figures and bare-headed bodies are pixel-identical, and they differ only in the head studies and the BARE-HEADED head. On identity they tie. Both show the inherited COURT drift (a glare and a stubble shadow), a FRONT face broader and heavier-jawed than V13's long, narrow face, and a LEFT PROFILE with a scooped, upturned nose instead of V13's long, straight nose. Even so, the views on each sheet still read as one man of the COURT figure's age, with black hair, the namam, pearl drops and an upturned moustache. f2-2 has the slightly better FRONT, which is narrower, with a thinner moustache that matches its other views. But f2-2 puts the knot at the back of the skull in LEFT PROFILE and almost fully behind the head in BARE-HEADED, which is the exact back-bun error fix2 was written to remove, and its BARE-HEADED face is a little more lined and older. That would mislead the panel generator on the knot rule. f2-1 places the knot correctly on the side of the head above the left ear in LEFT PROFILE, and its BARE-HEADED knot is closer to the ear, though it still protrudes. Its main flaw is a FRONT moustache that is still thick, which matches the COURT moustache and so does not change the man's identity. Adopt f2-1. If one more pass is affordable, ask it to thin the FRONT moustache and lower the FRONT and BARE-HEADED knots to ear-top height. Both candidates have clean, correctly spelled text: MARTHANDA VARMA, COURT, BARE-HEADED, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, BACK, and nothing extra. My zoom crops are in /tmp/claude-501/mvf2id/.

judgements.why: Both candidates pass several rules. The labels are exactly MARTHANDA VARMA, COURT, BARE-HEADED, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE and BACK, with no extra text. The hair is jet black with no grey (the highlights are only gloss). Every view has pearl drop earrings. The namam is a white U with a red centre in all bare-headed views. The BARE-HEADED figure has exactly two gold bead necklaces, a cream mundu with a gold border, a shoulder cloth and bare feet. The forearms are clean, with no brand or symbol (none is wanted for Varma). The background is plain ivory and the COURT figure is kept. The deciding rule is where the knot sits, which is the reason for the bare-headed views. In f2-1, LEFT PROFILE puts the knot inside the skull outline, just above and behind the left ear, as the base prompt asked. FRONT and BACK put it on his left side, so three of the four views agree on a left-side knot. In f2-2, both LEFT PROFILE and BARE-HEADED show a bun jutting out behind the skull, which fix2 explicitly bans, and f2-2 also has nape wisps. That would steer panels toward a back bun. f2-2's only edge is a slightly thinner moustache. Adopt f2-1 with these caveats: its BARE-HEADED knot sits high toward the rear, the knot is above ear-top height in FRONT and BACK, the brows are still a glare rather than calm, there is faint jaw stubble, and the moustache is medium rather than thin. Also, the COURT figure's curly locks below the turban (inherited from V13) break the never-curly lock, which the author may want to rule on.

A black moustache with curled tips, and nothing else on the face
The same warm brown skin tone and rendering
Black hair gathered into a knot (Pillai era, from ch17, and Varma bare-headed)
A gold ornament in the earlobe
A lean, muscular, bare-chested torso in the Kerala scenes, with a chain or necklace across the chest
A similar apparent age, a man in his thirties or forties
The same three-quarter, chin-raised heroic pose and line style on all three sheets
distinguishing_features: Forehead: Varma has a red-and-white vertical Vaishnavite mark, which still reads as a red stripe at 80 px. Nagoji's forehead is bare. This is the strongest single cue, but the bible's Varma base line does not require it (only the ch7 row does), so the generator can drop it.
Ear: Varma wears a large gold-capped pearl drop that hangs below the lobe and shows as a white dot beside the jaw at 80 px. Nagoji wears a tiny plain gold stud that almost disappears at panel size.
Grey: Ananthan Pillai has a clear white streak of grey at each temple. Varma's hair is all jet black with no grey.

Knot and hair texture: Pillai's topknot sits high on the crown, the hair is curly, and loose curls show at the nape. Varma's hair is sleek, straight and glossy, combed flat, with a small knot low on the left side above the left ear. In three-quarter view the two knots drift toward each other, and the ch11 war-hall headband hides Varma's knot completely.

Moustache: Nagoji's is thick, bushy and heavy and covers the upper lip. Varma's is slimmer and neatly trimmed with thin waxed upturned tips, and the upper lip shows. You can see this at 80 px, but it is subtle.

Face proportions: Nagoji's face is longer and gaunter, with hollow cheeks, heavy straight brows and a long neck. Varma's face is slightly broader and squarer, with arched brows and a frown crease. This is weak at panel size.
Build: Nagoji is a wiry rider with narrower shoulders. Varma has a broader chest and heavier arms. This is weak and is often hidden by framing.
Hair worn loose (commander era only): Nagoji's long curly black hair falls to the shoulders or shows under the rust-red turban. Varma's hair is never loose and never curly.

prompt_lines.nagoji: Nagoji has a long, lean, hollow-cheeked face with heavy straight brows, a thick bushy black moustache curled at the ends that hides his upper lip, curly black hair (loose to the shoulders as commander, or as Ananthan Pillai gathered in a topknot high on the crown with a white streak of grey at each temple), only a tiny plain gold stud in the earlobe, and a bare forehead with no mark.
prompt_lines.varma: Marthanda Varma has a broader, squarer face with arched brows, a slimmer, neatly trimmed moustache with thin upturned tips that leaves his upper lip showing, sleek, straight, glossy jet-black hair with no grey, combed flat and tied in a small knot low on the left side above his left ear and never on the crown, a large gold-capped pearl drop hanging from each earlobe, and a red-and-white vertical Vaishnavite mark on his forehead.

distinctness.verdict: Yes, a reader could take one man for the other. I cropped every head and shrank it to 80 px tall (crops in /tmp/claude-501/heads). With costume hidden, the faces themselves are the same template: oval face, high cheekbones, straight nose, clean square chin, curled moustache. On the current sheets, what separates them is a set of add-on markers: Varma's red-and-white forehead mark, his hanging pearl earrings, his sleek all-black hair with the knot at the side, and his thinner trimmed moustache, against Nagoji's bare forehead, tiny stud, grey temples, curly hair with the knot on the crown, and heavy bushy moustache. The generator has already dropped or swapped these markers on Varma, giving him grey temples, a crown knot and the heavy moustache, and then nothing in the face tells the two men apart.
